title.abbrev: YANG for RESTCONF Clients and Servers

front.title: A YANG Data Model for RESTCONF Clients and Servers

abstract.t: This document presents two YANG 1.1 modules: one module to configure a RESTCONF client and the other module to configure a RESTCONF server. These modules support both standard RESTCONF and RESTCONF Call Home connections.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: This document presents two YANG 1.1. modules : one module to configure a RESTCONF client and the other module to configure a RESTCONF server. These modules support both standard RESTCONF and RESTCONF Call Home connections .

Both modules support HTTPS, RESTCONF's required transport, whether by TLS or QUIC . The YANG module configuring RESTCONF servers additionally supports HTTP, enabling the RESTCONF server to be deployed behind a TLS-terminator.

section.name: Relation to Other RFCs
section.t: This document presents two YANG 1.1 modules that belong to a collection of RFCs that are designed to work together. Ultimately, these modules support the configuration of clients and servers for both the Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF) and RESTCONF protocol .

Primary dependency relationships between the YANG groupings defined in the various RFCs are presented in the below diagram. In some cases, a document may define secondary groupings that introduce dependencies not illustrated in the diagram. The labels in the diagram are a shorthand name for the defining RFC. The citation reference for the shorthand name is provided in .

Please note that the arrows in the diagram point from referencer to referenced. For example, the "crypto-types" RFC does not have any dependencies, whilst the "keystore" RFC depends on the "crypto-types" RFC.

section.name: The "ietf-restconf-client" YANG Module
section.t: The RESTCONF client YANG data model presented in this section supports both clients initiating connections to servers and clients listening for connections from servers calling home.
YANG feature statements are used to enable implementations to advertise which potentially uncommon parts of the data model the RESTCONF client supports.

section.t: This section provides an overview of the "ietf-restconf-client" YANG module in terms of its features and groupings.

section.name: Groupings
section.t: The "ietf-restconf-client" module defines the following "grouping" statements:
Each of these groupings are presented in the following subsections.

section.name: The "restconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping" Grouping
section.t: The following tree diagram illustrates the "restconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping" grouping:
section.sourcecode: grouping restconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping: +-- http-client-parameters | +---u httpc:http-client-grouping +-- restconf-client-parameters +---u rcc:restconf-client-grouping
section.t: Comments:

ul.li: The "restconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping" defines the configuration for a full RESTCONF protocol stack for RESTCONF clients that initiate connections to RESTCONF servers (as opposed to receiving call home connections).
The "restconf-client-grouping" grouping is discussed in in this document.

section.name: The "restconf-client-listen-stack-grouping" Grouping
section.t: The following tree diagram illustrates the "restconf-client-listen-stack-grouping" grouping:
section.sourcecode: grouping restconf-client-listen-stack-grouping: +-- (transport) +--:(tcp) {tcp-listen}? +-- tcp +-- tcp-server-parameters | +---u tcps:tcp-server-grouping +-- http-client-parameters | +---u httpc:http-client-grouping +-- restconf-client-parameters +---u rcc:restconf-client-grouping
section.t: Comments:

ul.li: The "restconf-client-listen-stack-grouping" defines the configuration for a full RESTCONF protocol stack for RESTCONF clients that receive call home connections from RESTCONF servers.

The "transport" choice node selects the HTTP-level transport to configure, with each case enabled by a "feature" statement. The "tcp" case is used for HTTP up to and including HTTP/2. Other transports MAY be augmented into the "transport" choice node by future efforts.

section.name: The "restconf-client-app-grouping" Grouping
section.t: The following tree diagram illustrates the "restconf-client-app-grouping" grouping:
section.sourcecode: grouping restconf-client-app-grouping: +-- initiate! {initiate}? | +-- restconf-server* [name] | +-- name string | +-- endpoints | | +-- endpoint* [name] | | +-- name string | | +---u restconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping | +-- connection-type | | +-- (connection-type) | | +--:(persistent-connection) | | | +-- persistent! | | +--:(periodic-connection) | | +-- periodic! | | +-- period? uint16 | | +-- anchor-time? yang:date-and-time | | +-- idle-timeout? uint16 | +-- reconnect-strategy | +-- start-with? enumeration | +-- max-wait? uint16 | +-- max-attempts? uint8 +-- listen! {listen}? +-- idle-timeout? uint16 +-- endpoints +-- endpoint* [name] +-- name string +---u restconf-client-listen-stack-grouping
section.t: Comments:

ul.li: The "restconf-client-app-grouping" defines the configuration for a RESTCONF client that supports both initiating connections to RESTCONF servers and receiving call home connections from RESTCONF servers.
Both the "initiate" and "listen" subtrees are predicated by "feature" statements.

section.t: The following tree diagram lists all the protocol-accessible nodes defined in the "ietf-restconf-client" module:
Comments:

ul.li: Protocol-accessible nodes are those nodes that are accessible when the module is "implemented", as described in .

section.name: The "restconf-server-grouping" Grouping
section.t: The following tree diagram illustrates the "restconf-server-grouping" grouping:
Comments:

ul.li: The "restconf-server-grouping" defines the configuration for the "RESTCONF" part of a protocol stack. It does not, for instance, define any configuration for the "TCP", "TLS", or "HTTP" protocol layers (for that, see Sections and ).
The "client-identity-mappings" node defines a mapping from certificate fields to RESTCONF user names.

ul.li: The "restconf-server-listen-stack-grouping" defines the configuration for a full RESTCONF protocol stack for RESTCONF servers that listen for connections from RESTCONF clients (as opposed to initiating call home connections).

The "transport" choice node selects the HTTP-level transport to configure, with each case enabled by a "feature" statement. section.name: Considerations for the "ietf-restconf-client" YANG Module
section.t: This section is modeled after the template described in .

The "ietf-restconf-client" YANG module defines a data model that is designed to be accessed via YANG-based management protocols, such as the Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF) and RESTCONF . These YANG-based management protocols (1) have to use a secure transport layer (e.g., Secure Shell (SSH) Transport Layer ) and (2) have to use mutual authentication (e.g., SSH Authentication Protocol , TLS , and QUIC ).

The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) provides the means to restrict access for particular NETCONF or RESTCONF users to a preconfigured subset of all available NETCONF or RESTCONF protocol operations and content.

None of the writable data nodes defined in this YANG module are considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. The NACM "default-deny-write" extension has not been set for any data nodes defined in this module.

None of the readable data nodes defined in this YANG module are considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. The NACM "default-deny-all" extension has not been set for any data nodes defined in this module.
This YANG module does not define any RPCs, actions, or notifications; thus, the security consideration for such is not provided here.

This YANG module uses groupings from other YANG modules that define nodes that may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. For information as to which nodes may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments, refer to the Security Considerations of , , and other RFCs defining nodes upon which this module relies.
This YANG module uses groupings defined in other RFCs that define data nodes that do set the NACM "default-deny-all" and "default-deny-write" extensions.

This YANG module enables the possibility for a RESTCONF client to open a port to listen for non-TLS-based RESTCONF Call Home connections . Whilst RESTCONF requires HTTPS, this configuration is provided for deployments having a TLS-terminator (e.g., a load balancer) in front of the TLS client. In such a case, the security boundary extends to the TLS-terminator.

section.t: This section is modeled after the template described in .

The "ietf-restconf-server" YANG module defines a data model that is designed to be accessed via YANG-based management protocols, such as the Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF) and RESTCONF . These YANG-based management protocols (1) have to use a secure transport layer (e.g., Secure Shell (SSH) Transport Layer ) and (2) have to use mutual authentication (e.g., SSH Authentication Protocol , TLS , and QUIC ).

The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) provides the means to restrict access for particular NETCONF or RESTCONF users to a preconfigured subset of all available NETCONF or RESTCONF protocol operations and content.

None of the writable data nodes in this YANG module are considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. The NACM "default-deny-write" extension has not been set for any data nodes defined in this module.

None of the readable data nodes in this YANG module are considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. The NACM "default-deny-all" extension has not been set for any data nodes defined in this module.
This YANG module does not define any RPCs, actions, or notifications; thus, the security consideration for such is not provided here.

This YANG module uses groupings from other YANG modules that define nodes that may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. Refer to the Security Considerations of , , , , and for information as to which nodes may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments.
This YANG module uses groupings defined in other RFCs that define data nodes that do set the NACM "default-deny-all" and "default-deny-write" extensions.

This YANG module enables the possibility for a RESTCONF server to open a port to listen for non-TLS-based RESTCONF connections. Whilst RESTCONF requires HTTPS, this configuration is provided to support deploying a TLS-terminator (e.g., a load balancer) in front of the TLS server. In such a case, the security boundary extends to the TLS-terminator.
